docs.title: flinch
docs.text:
Solar flares in Sun-as-a-star radial velocities.

Do solar flares contaminate the radial-velocity detection of Earth analogues?

To find a planet like the Earth around a star like the Sun, the velocity of the star has to be measured to about 10 cm/s: the Earth moves the Sun by 9 cm/s. Some of the spectrographs built for that also observe the Sun every clear day, as if it were a distant star. This project cross-matches those solar velocities with the flares recorded by the GOES satellites and asks:

  1. Does a flare move the radial velocity of the Sun seen as a star?
  2. From which flare size, and by how much?
  3. What does that mean for planet searches?

It uses two instruments that watch the Sun at different hours and therefore see different flares: NEID (Arizona) and HARPS-N (La Palma).

docs.title: The answer
docs.text:
Solar flares do not significantly contaminate the detection of Earth analogues by radial velocity. This has been shown for the Sun, not for Sun-like stars in general.

Question Answer Evidence Does the velocity change during a flare? No, within 7 cm/s 254 measurements of 253 flares of class M and X: −0.029 ± 0.026 m/s. NEID alone: −0.035 ± 0.035 (139 flares). HARPS-N alone: −0.021 ± 0.039 (115) Do larger flares move it more? No 18 flares of class X: −0.074 ± 0.072 m/s. No change, but the limit, 0.2 m/s, is twice the signal of the Earth Is there a rotation signature (opposite sign east and west)? No −0.006 ± 0.038 m/s for an X1 flare at the limb, within a factor of 1.5 to 3.5 of the largest shift expected Would a signal have been seen? Yes 98 % of a shift added to the data is measured back Do the spectra see the flares at all? Yes Ca II H and K and H alpha brighten in all 14 flares on the disc with spectra, by 2 to 5 parts per thousand How much of the time is the Sun flaring? 1.6 % 358 flares of class M or X per year on average from 2020 to 2026, counted from start to end (19 minutes in the median); 3.8 % in 2024, the most active year

The Sun does not flinch, but it blushes: the chromospheric lines brighten while the velocity stays put. See Results.

docs.title: Where the data go
docs.text:
Downloads go to data/ inside the repository, or to the folder named by the environment variable FLINCH_DATA. Tables go to results/ and figures to docs/web/img/.

Spectra are heavy to download

A level-2 NEID spectrum is 113 MB and the archive does not serve byte ranges, so each one is downloaded whole, reduced to a 0.2 MB extract and deleted. A campaign of 700 spectra moves 80 GB through the network and keeps 140 MB. The computer must stay awake: on a laptop, keep it plugged in and with the lid open.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
The measurement has four steps. The figure shows them for one flare.

Left: the X1.3 flare of 30 March 2022. Right: one of its control days, the same hour a day later. Top: X-ray flux. Bottom: NEID velocities after removing the trend of the day, one point per spectrum. The grey band is the window before the flare and the blue band the window during its rise; the thick lines are the mean velocity in each. One flare or one control changes by tens of cm/s by chance; only the average over many flares, compared with their controls, reaches the precision needed.

  1. Clean the velocities: drop those taken through clouds and remove the slow trend of each day.
  2. For each flare, take the mean velocity during its rise minus the mean velocity just before it.
  3. Repeat step 2 on days without flares, at the same hour (the controls), and subtract their mean change from that of the flare.
  4. Average over all the flares.

docs.title: Step 1: cleaning the velocities
docs.text:
A cloud that covers part of the rotating disc shifts the velocity by tens of m/s. For NEID a spectrum is kept when its signal-to-noise ratio is within 1 % of that of its neighbours, its velocity error is below 1 m/s and its velocity is within five standard deviations of the trend of the day. For HARPS-N the quality flag of its data release is used (above 0.99).

The velocity drifts slowly through the day, because of the rotation of the Earth and of the changing height of the Sun. A polynomial of degree 2 is fitted to each day and subtracted. Days with too few good velocities, or with a scatter above 1.5 m/s, are dropped.

docs.title: Step 2: the velocity change of a flare
docs.text:
Window Limits Before From 40 to 5 minutes before the start of the flare During From the start to 2 minutes after the X-ray peak (the rise of the flare)

Δv = mean velocity during − mean velocity before

A flare counts only if both windows hold at least 70 % of the velocities expected.

Step NEID HARPS-N M and X flares in the years of the instrument 2122 1750 With both windows complete 140 122 With at least three controls 139 115

docs.title: Step 3: the controls
docs.text:
The velocity of the Sun changes all the time, flare or no flare. To know what a flare adds, the same two windows are measured on other days at the same hour, up to 15 days before and after, with no M or X flare within 45 minutes. Shifting by whole days keeps the height of the Sun and the daily cycle of the instrument.

d = Δv of the flare − mean Δv of its controls

If flares do nothing to the velocity, d averages to zero.

docs.title: Step 4: averages
docs.text:
Number Definition What it tests Mean change Mean of d Any shift common to the flares Shift of an X1 flare, S Σ f d / Σ f² A shift that grows with the size of the flare Rotation term, R Σ (f v) d / Σ (f v)² A shift with the sign of the side of the disc

f is the size of the flare, its peak flux in units of X1 (0.1 for M1, 2 for X2). v is its position: the rotation velocity at the flare as a fraction of that at the limb (−1 at the east limb, +1 at the west limb).

The rotation term is the one test whose sign can be predicted. A flare is a bright patch on a rotating disc, so it should shift the velocity by

shift ≈ (ΔF / F) · v_rot · K

where ΔF / F is the fraction by which the flare brightens the Sun in visible light, v_rot the rotation velocity at the flare (up to 1845 m/s at the limb, as seen from the Earth) and K a factor between 0 and 1. K is 1 if the extra light carries the same absorption lines as the surface under it, and 0 if it is light without lines, which only makes the lines of the rest of the disc shallower.

docs.title: Errors, limits and sensitivity
docs.text:
• Errors. Flares of the same day are not independent. The calculation is repeated thousands of times with a random selection of the observing days (a bootstrap); the spread of the results is the error.
  • Limits. When a result x with error σ is compatible with zero, the largest value it could hide with 95 % confidence is |x| + 1.645 σ.
  • Two instruments. They are combined by weighting each with the inverse of the square of its error.
  • Sensitivity. A known shift is added to the published velocities during the "during" window of control epochs, and the whole measurement is repeated.

docs.title: The spectra
docs.text: Each NEID spectrum comes with indices that measure how bright the cores of chromospheric lines are. The response of an index to a flare is its mean from 8 minutes before the X-ray peak to 10 minutes after it, minus its mean before the start. The same is measured in control windows. See NEID spectra.

docs.title: What was fixed when
docs.text: The quality cuts were chosen from the noise of the controls and the number of flares, never from the result. The windows were fixed after a first look at the NEID data, not before; the robustness table shows the result with the alternatives. HARPS-N was analysed afterwards, once, with the choices already made.

The data release used here as second instrument. It cites Pietrow et al. (2024) as having shown that flares contribute negligibly to the velocity of quiet Sun-like stars; their limit was 50 cm/s, more than five times the signal of the Earth.

  • Liu, X., et al. (2025). Sun-as-a-star analysis of the solar eruption source region using H alpha spectroscopic observations of CHASE. The Astrophysical Journal, 993, 126.
  • Yu, H. C., et al. (2025). Sun-as-a-star analysis of simulated solar flares. Astronomy & Astrophysics, 694, A315.

  • Zhang, J., et al. (2026). Can we distinguish the source region location of filament/prominence eruptions from the Sun-as-a-star H alpha spectrum? The Astrophysical Journal, 1004, 66.
  • Xu, Y., et al. (2022). Sun-as-a-star spectroscopic observations of the line-of-sight velocity of a solar eruption on 2021 October 28. The Astrophysical Journal, 931, 76.

These are studies of single events, of a few events or of simulations, most of them in H alpha from imaging spectrographs: the spectra are integrated over a region around the flare and normalised by the light of the disc. Otsu et al. (2026) gather 34 flares, but measure in images when the postflare loops appear. Only the first of the list above measures radial velocities, for two flares: an upper limit of 50 cm/s and a request for a statistical follow-up. The last two measure, in extreme-ultraviolet lines, the velocity of the material ejected in eruptions (about 400 km/s along the line of sight in the event of Xu et al., and eight ejections in twelve years of data in Lu et al.). That is the velocity of the ejecta, not of the photospheric spectrum from which the radial velocity of a star is measured.

docs.title: Velocities inside the flaring area
docs.text:
These works look at the velocity where the flare is, in resolved images or in simulations, not at the velocity of the whole disc.

  • Saar, S. H., Palumbo, M. L., Haywood, R. D., & Dupree, A. K. (2018). A first look at the effect of flares on radial velocity jitter in G dwarfs: a punch and a splash? Poster at Cool Stars 20, doi:10.5281/zenodo.1490103. Pixels flagged as flares in SDO images of 2014 (more than four times as bright as the quiet Sun at 170 nm) are shifted by about 160 m/s to the red near the disc centre and by 130 to 220 m/s to the blue near the limb. Over the year they cover 0.04 % of the disc, and in the authors' tentative model only 29 % of them follow the catalogued flares.
  • Monson, A. J., et al. (2021). Flare-induced photospheric velocity diagnostics. The Astrophysical Journal, 915, 16. Simulations: chromospheric emission makes photospheric Fe I lines look shifted by up to 40 m/s.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Status: November 2026. The velocity is measured with two instruments, NEID and HARPS-N. The spectra are those of NEID: 23 flares and nine flare-free control windows.

docs.title: The velocity of the Sun does not change during flares
docs.text:
Two instruments that watched different flares give the same answer.

Change of the velocity during the flare, minus that of its controls, in m/s (in brackets, the number of flares):

NEID HARPS-N Both 95 % limit Mean change, all M and X flares −0.035 ± 0.035 (139) −0.021 ± 0.039 (115) −0.029 ± 0.026 (254) 0.07 Mean change, M class −0.032 ± 0.039 (128) −0.015 ± 0.042 (108) −0.025 ± 0.028 (236) 0.07 Mean change, X class −0.060 ± 0.088 (11) −0.104 ± 0.127 (7) −0.074 ± 0.072 (18) 0.19 Shift of an X1 flare, S −0.010 ± 0.061 −0.005 ± 0.040 −0.006 ± 0.033 0.06 Rotation term, R −0.106 ± 0.082 +0.022 ± 0.043 −0.006 ± 0.038 0.07

Together the mean change is below 0.07 m/s, less than the 0.09 m/s that the Earth imprints on the Sun. The 254 measurements are of 253 different flares: one was observed by both instruments. The flares used are a fair sample of all the M and X flares: their classes and their positions on the disc are distributed like those of the full list (Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, p between 0.08 and 0.96). With as few flares as in the X-class row, the error is itself uncertain by a quarter.

Three further checks give the same answer:

  • Larger flares do not shift the velocity more. For the 18 flares of class X no change is found either, but the limit, 0.19 m/s, is twice the signal of the Earth.
  • There are no shifts of opposite sign that cancel in the mean. The changes of the flares scatter as much as those of the controls: 0.40 m/s for both with NEID, 0.41 with HARPS-N.
  • There is no rotation signature. The rotation term is below 0.07 m/s for an X1 flare at the limb, which means K · ΔF / F < 3.7 × 10⁻⁵ per X1 flare (see Method).

docs.title: The same spectra do see the flares
docs.text:
A result of "nothing happens" needs the proof that the instrument was looking. The spectra give it: the chromospheric lines brighten as the X-ray flux rises, peak a few minutes after the X-ray peak and are still bright 40 minutes later. In the control windows they stay flat, and in those same spectra the velocity does not move.

Mean response of the flares on the disc (within 0.9 solar radii of the centre), from 8 minutes before the X-ray peak to 10 minutes after it:

X class (8 flares) M5 to M9 (6 flares) Controls (9 windows) Ca II H and K (parts per thousand) +5.3 ± 1.7 +2.2 ± 0.4 0.0 ± 0.2 H alpha core (parts per thousand) +3.3 ± 1.1 +2.0 ± 0.2 −0.1 ± 0.2 Velocity (m/s) −0.11 ± 0.21 −0.10 ± 0.11 +0.07 ± 0.27
  • All 14 flares on the disc brighten in both lines.
  • Smaller flares respond less: those between M5 and M9, about half as much as those of class X.
  • Near the limb the response is weaker: +1.7 ± 0.9 in Ca II H and K for four X-class flares, +1.4 ± 0.5 for five between M5 and M9.
  • Weaker flares were not fetched. Between M2 and M5 the response of one flare would be below the noise, and these 14 already show that the spectra see the flares.

The table flare by flare is results/spectral_response.csv. One flare in detail, the X6.3 of 22 February 2024, whose peak came just after the last solar spectrum of that day:

docs.title: What was to be expected
docs.text:
• How bright is a flare in visible light? At the peak of an average M2 flare the Sun brightens by 7 parts per million, and in the X17 flare of 28 October 2003 it brightened by 264 (Kretzschmar 2011). Those classes are on the old GOES scale, which carried a factor 0.7; on the scale used here they give 11 to 23 parts per million for an X1 flare. The two agree within a factor of two although the flares differ by a factor of almost ninety in class: on average the visible brightening grows with the X-ray class, though not flare by flare.
  • How much does that light move the velocity? At most 2 to 4 cm/s for an X1 flare at the limb (K = 1), and less elsewhere.
  • How close do we get? The limit of the two instruments together is 1.5 to 3.5 times that. The absence of a rotation signal is what the physics predicts; it is now measured.
  • And the lines of the flaring area itself? In resolved images they are shifted by up to 200 m/s (Saar et al. 2018). A ten-thousandth of the disc shifted by 100 m/s moves the velocity of the whole Sun by about 1 cm/s, so this effect depends on the area of the flare, which has not been estimated here. The limit on the mean change bounds it from the data.

docs.title: The answer
docs.text:
Solar flares do not significantly contaminate the detection of Earth analogues by radial velocity, for two reasons:

  • They move the velocity very little: less than 7 cm/s on average up to class X. For class X alone no change is found either, but the limit is about 20 cm/s, twice the signal of the Earth.
  • They take up little of the time. Between December 2020 and November 2026, six years that span the rise and the maximum of cycle 25, the Sun produced 358 flares of class M or X per year on average, 18 of them of class X. Counting each flare from its start to its end in the GOES list (19 minutes in the median), the Sun spent 1.6 % of the time in one of them (0.1 % for class X). In 2024, the most active year, there were 934 flares, 52 of them of class X, and the Sun spent 3.8 % of the time in one (0.3 % for class X).

This has been shown for the Sun, not for Sun-like stars in general: stars more active than the Sun, with larger and more frequent flares, are another matter.

docs.title: How this compares with published work
docs.text:
• Velocity. Pietrow et al. (2024) followed two X-class flares of 6 September 2017 with HARPS-N. They could not claim a detection: they set an upper limit of 50 cm/s and asked for a statistical follow-up. Here the mean change of 253 flares seen by two instruments is below 7 cm/s. The larger of their two flares is in the HARPS-N sample: its change is −0.01 m/s, with a single-flare error of 0.41 m/s.
  • Chromosphere. In the same two flares Ca II H and K rose by more than 1 %. Here Ca II H and K is also the most sensitive index, up to 1.7 %.
  • Light of the whole disc. The H alpha studies with imaging spectrographs (Otsu et al. 2022, 2024; Ma et al. 2024) integrate a region around the flare and normalise by the disc. NEID records the response in the light of the whole disc, and the control windows give its noise floor.

docs.title: An excess before the X-class flares of NEID that HARPS-N does not see
docs.text: In the ten minutes from 60 to 50 minutes before the X-ray peak, the X-class flares observed by NEID sit 0.44 ± 0.11 m/s above the trend of their day (19 flares with data at that time, 17 of them positive). It was noticed in the mean velocities, not predicted. It is absent in the M-class flares of NEID (0.00 ± 0.03 m/s) and in the controls, and HARPS-N does not show it: −0.12 ± 0.11 m/s for its ten X-class flares, which are other flares. The origin of the feature is unclear. If it were a general property of X-class flares, the HARPS-N sample should show it too; its absence there points to the instrument or to chance, although a solar origin cannot be excluded.

def read_flloc(path: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Read a flare location file: one row per ``flare_id`` with its position on the disc.

    ``x_norm`` and ``y_norm`` are helioprojective coordinates in units of the solar radius
    (x positive towards the west limb, the receding one). ``r_norm`` is the distance to the disc
    centre. Positions come from the quadrant diode of the X-ray sensor and are unreliable for
    weak flares; entries without a position are NaN. ``car_lon`` is the Carrington longitude,
    which stays fixed for a region as the Sun rotates.
    """
    with h5py.File(path, "r") as handle:
        xy = handle["flloc_xy"][:].astype(float)
        radius = handle["solar_radius"][:].astype(float)
        hg = handle["flloc_hg"][:].astype(float)
        carrington = handle["flloc_car"][:].astype(float)
        flare_id = handle["flare_id"][:]
    xy[xy < -9000.0] = np.nan
    hg[hg < -9000.0] = np.nan
    carrington[carrington < -9000.0] = np.nan
    table = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "flare_id": flare_id,
            "x_norm": xy[:, 0] / radius,
            "y_norm": xy[:, 1] / radius,
            "lon": hg[:, 0],
            "lat": hg[:, 1],
            "car_lon": carrington[:, 0],
        }
    )
    table["r_norm"] = np.hypot(table["x_norm"], table["y_norm"])
    return table.drop_duplicates("flare_id")

def read_flsum(path: Path, satellite: int | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Read a flare summary file into one row per flare.

    The file stores one record per event marker (start, peak, end) sharing a ``flare_id``.
    Times are Julian dates (UTC); fluxes are in W m^-2 (1-8 Angstrom), fluences in J m^-2.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    with h5py.File(path, "r") as handle:
        records = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "jd": JD_J2000 + handle["time"][:] / 86400.0,
                "status": handle["status"].asstr()[:],
                "goes_class": handle["flare_class"].asstr()[:],
                "flux": handle["xrsb_flux"][:].astype(float),
                "fluence": handle["integrated_flux"][:].astype(float),
                "flare_id": handle["flare_id"][:],
            }
        )
    if satellite is None:
        match = re.search(r"_g(\d\d)_", path.name)
        satellite = int(match.group(1)) if match else 0

    def marker(status: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return records[records["status"] == status].drop_duplicates("flare_id").set_index("flare_id")

    peaks, starts, ends = marker("EVENT_PEAK"), marker("EVENT_START"), marker("EVENT_END")
    peaks = peaks[peaks["goes_class"] != ""]
    flares = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "jd_start": starts["jd"].reindex(peaks.index),
            "jd_peak": peaks["jd"],
            "jd_end": ends["jd"].reindex(peaks.index),
            "goes_class": peaks["goes_class"],
            "peak_flux": peaks["flux"],
            "fluence": ends["fluence"].reindex(peaks.index),
        }
    )
    flares["satellite"] = satellite
    return flares.reset_index().sort_values("jd_peak", ignore_index=True)

Two entries are the same flare when their peaks are closer than tolerance_min minutes, or when the secondary peak falls between the start and the end of a primary flare (the two satellites can place the peak of a long, flat flare several minutes apart).

def merge_flare_lists(primary: pd.DataFrame, secondary: pd.DataFrame, tolerance_min: float = 3.0) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The primary list plus the flares of the secondary with no counterpart in the primary.

    Two entries are the same flare when their peaks are closer than ``tolerance_min`` minutes,
    or when the secondary peak falls between the start and the end of a primary flare (the two
    satellites can place the peak of a long, flat flare several minutes apart).
    """
    if primary.empty or secondary.empty:
        return pd.concat([primary, secondary], ignore_index=True).sort_values("jd_peak", ignore_index=True)
    peaks = np.sort(primary["jd_peak"].to_numpy())
    candidates = secondary["jd_peak"].to_numpy()
    index = np.searchsorted(peaks, candidates)
    before = np.abs(candidates - peaks[np.clip(index - 1, 0, len(peaks) - 1)])
    after = np.abs(peaks[np.clip(index, 0, len(peaks) - 1)] - candidates)
    isolated = np.minimum(before, after) > tolerance_min * MINUTE
    if {"jd_start", "jd_end"} <= set(primary.columns):
        windows = primary.dropna(subset=["jd_start", "jd_end"]).sort_values("jd_start")
        if not windows.empty:
            starts, ends = windows["jd_start"].to_numpy(), windows["jd_end"].to_numpy()
            last_started = np.searchsorted(starts, candidates, side="right") - 1
            inside = (last_started >= 0) & (candidates <= ends[np.clip(last_started, 0, len(ends) - 1)])
            isolated &= ~inside
    merged = pd.concat([primary, secondary[isolated]], ignore_index=True)
    return merged.sort_values("jd_peak", ignore_index=True)

    """Merged flare list from the downloaded summaries (run ``python -m flinch download`` first)."""
    directory = Path(directory or data_dir() / "goes")

        files = sorted(directory.glob(f"sci_xrsf-l2-flsum_g{satellite}_*.nc"))

            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"no GOES-{satellite} flare summary in {directory}; run `python -m flinch download`"

Add jd_impulsive: the time of the steepest rise of the X-ray flux of each flare.

The time derivative of the soft X-ray flux follows the energy deposition by accelerated particles (the Neupert effect), so its maximum marks the impulsive phase better than the X-ray peak, which comes minutes later. It is searched between the start and the peak with a centred difference over two minutes; flares without one-minute data keep NaN.

def add_impulsive_time(flares: pd.DataFrame, directory: Path | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Add ``jd_impulsive``: the time of the steepest rise of the X-ray flux of each flare.

    The time derivative of the soft X-ray flux follows the energy deposition by accelerated
    particles (the Neupert effect), so its maximum marks the impulsive phase better than the
    X-ray peak, which comes minutes later. It is searched between the start and the peak with a
    centred difference over two minutes; flares without one-minute data keep NaN.
    """
    out = flares.copy()
    out["jd_impulsive"] = np.nan
    start = out["jd_start"].fillna(out["jd_peak"] - 10.0 * MINUTE)
    years = jd_to_datetime(out["jd_peak"]).year
    for (satellite, year), rows in out.groupby([out["satellite"], years]):
        try:
            jd, flux = load_avg1m(int(satellite), int(year), directory)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  (a missing year leaves NaN)
            continue
        slope = np.full(len(flux), np.nan)
        slope[1:-1] = (flux[2:] - flux[:-2]) / 2.0
        for index in rows.index:
            first, last = np.searchsorted(jd, [start[index] - 0.5 * MINUTE, out.at[index, "jd_peak"] + 0.5 * MINUTE])
            if last - first >= 2 and np.any(np.isfinite(slope[first:last])):
                out.at[index, "jd_impulsive"] = jd[first + int(np.nanargmax(slope[first:last]))] + 0.5 * MINUTE
    return out

Add coverage columns to a flare table.

n_peak: observations within peak_tolerance_min of the flare peak. n_pre: observations in the baseline_min minutes before the flare start. n_post: observations in the baseline_min minutes after the peak. at_peak: the instrument was observing at the peak. well_covered: at the peak, with at least min_points observations before and after.

def add_coverage(
    flares: pd.DataFrame,
    observation_jd,
    peak_tolerance_min: float = 2.0,
    baseline_min: float = 30.0,
    min_points: int = 5,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Add coverage columns to a flare table.

    ``n_peak``: observations within ``peak_tolerance_min`` of the flare peak.
    ``n_pre``: observations in the ``baseline_min`` minutes before the flare start.
    ``n_post``: observations in the ``baseline_min`` minutes after the peak.
    ``at_peak``: the instrument was observing at the peak.
    ``well_covered``: at the peak, with at least ``min_points`` observations before and after.

    A flare without a recorded start is assumed to start 10 minutes before its peak.
    """
    times = np.sort(np.asarray(observation_jd, dtype=float))
    out = flares.copy()
    peak = out["jd_peak"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    start = out["jd_start"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    start = np.where(np.isfinite(start), start, peak - 10.0 * MINUTE)
    out["n_peak"] = count_between(times, peak - peak_tolerance_min * MINUTE, peak + peak_tolerance_min * MINUTE)
    out["n_pre"] = count_between(times, start - baseline_min * MINUTE, start)
    out["n_post"] = count_between(times, peak, peak + baseline_min * MINUTE)
    out["at_peak"] = out["n_peak"] > 0
    out["well_covered"] = out["at_peak"] & (out["n_pre"] >= min_points) & (out["n_post"] >= min_points)
    return out

def summarize(flares: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:

def extract(path: Path) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Compact extract of a level-2 file, as a dictionary of arrays ready for ``numpy.savez``.

    Keys: the header values in ``HEADER_KEYS`` and ``CCF_KEYS`` (lower case); ``activity_names``,
    ``activity_values`` and ``activity_errors`` (the indices computed by the NEID pipeline);
    ``ccf`` (sum over orders of the cross-correlation function, on the velocity grid
    ``ccfstart + ccfstep * i`` km/s); and for each window in ``LINE_WINDOWS`` the arrays
    ``<name>_wave``, ``<name>_flux`` and ``<name>_var``.
    """
    from astropy.io import fits  # optional dependency ("analysis" extra)

    out: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    with fits.open(path, memmap=True) as hdus:
        primary = hdus[0].header
        for key in HEADER_KEYS:
            out[key.lower()] = np.float64(primary.get(key, np.nan))
        ccf_header = hdus["CCFS"].header
        for key in CCF_KEYS:
            out[key.lower()] = np.float64(ccf_header.get(key, np.nan))
        out["ccf"] = np.nansum(np.asarray(hdus["CCFS"].data, dtype=float), axis=0)
        activity = hdus["ACTIVITY"].data
        out["activity_names"] = np.array([str(name).strip() for name in activity["INDEX"]])
        out["activity_values"] = np.asarray(activity["VALUE"], dtype=float)
        out["activity_errors"] = np.asarray(activity["UNCERTAINTY"], dtype=float)
        wave = np.asarray(hdus["SCIWAVESTITCH"].data, dtype=float)
        flux = hdus["SCIFLUXSTITCH"].data
        variance = hdus["SCIVARSTITCH"].data
        for name, (low, high) in LINE_WINDOWS.items():
            first, last = np.searchsorted(wave, [low, high])
            out[f"{name}_wave"] = wave[first:last]
            out[f"{name}_flux"] = np.asarray(flux[first:last], dtype=np.float32)
            out[f"{name}_var"] = np.asarray(variance[first:last], dtype=np.float32)
    return out

def fetch_one(filepath: str, filename: str, directory: Path, scratch: Path) -> Path:
    """Download one level-2 file, save its extract in ``directory`` and delete the file."""
    destination = directory / (Path(filename).stem + ".npz")
    if destination.exists():
        return destination
    raw = _retry(lambda: download(f"{FILE_URL}?filehand={filepath}&solar", scratch / filename, overwrite=True), attempts=3)
    try:
        arrays = extract(raw)
        partial = destination.with_name(destination.stem + ".part.npz")  # savez needs the .npz suffix
        np.savez_compressed(partial, **arrays)
        _retry(lambda: partial.replace(destination))
    finally:
        _retry(lambda: raw.unlink(missing_ok=True))
    return destination

def fetch_window(jd_from: float, jd_to: float, name: str, workers: int = 3, step: int = 1) -> Path:
    """Fetch the extracts of every solar spectrum in a time window; returns their directory.

    Extracts go to ``<data>/spectra/<name>/``. Files already extracted are skipped, so an
    interrupted run can simply be repeated. A file that fails is reported and left for a rerun.
    With ``step`` = n only every n-th spectrum is fetched: a quick first pass at lower cadence,
    which a later run with a smaller step completes.
    """
    directory = data_dir() / "spectra" / name
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    files = list_files(jd_from, jd_to).iloc[::step]
    scratch = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "flinch_spectra"
    scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def task(row) -> str | None:
        try:
            fetch_one(row.l2filepath, row.l2filename, directory, scratch)
            return None
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001  (reported; the rest of the window goes on)
            return f"{row.l2filename}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
        failures = [message for message in pool.map(task, files.itertuples()) if message]
    done = len(list(directory.glob("neidL2_*.npz")))
    print(f"{name}: {done} of {len(files)} spectra extracted in {directory}", flush=True)
    for message in failures:
        print(f"  failed  {message}", flush=True)
    return directory

def load_window(directory: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
    """Read the extracts of a window.

    Returns a table with one row per spectrum (time, velocity, every activity index and its
    error as ``<index>_err``) and a dictionary with the stacked arrays: ``ccf`` and, for each
    line window, ``<name>_wave``, ``<name>_flux`` and ``<name>_var`` (spectra along the first axis,
    truncated to the shortest window, whose length can differ by a pixel between spectra).
    """
    rows, arrays = [], {}
    for path in sorted(Path(directory).glob("neidL2_*.npz")):
        with np.load(path, allow_pickle=False) as data:
            row = {"file": path.stem, "obsjd": float(data["obsjd"])}
            row["jd"] = row["obsjd"] + 0.5 * float(data["exptime"]) / 86400.0
            row["rv_ms"] = float(data["ccfrvmod"]) * 1000.0
            row["sunagl"] = float(data["sunagl"])
            for index, value, error in zip(data["activity_names"], data["activity_values"], data["activity_errors"]):
                row[str(index)] = float(value)
                row[f"{index}_err"] = float(error)
            rows.append(row)
            for key in data.files:
                if key == "ccf" or key.endswith(("_wave", "_flux", "_var")):
                    arrays.setdefault(key, []).append(np.asarray(data[key], dtype=float))
    stacked = {}
    for key, values in arrays.items():
        length = min(len(v) for v in values)
        stacked[key] = np.vstack([v[:length] for v in values])
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), stacked

def select_events(min_class: str = "M1.0", max_class: str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flares observed at the peak or during the rise, strongest first.

    ``max_class`` is exclusive: ``select_events("M5.0", "X1.0")`` gives the flares from M5.0 up
    to, but not including, X1.0.
    """
    observations = neid.read_solar_table()
    jd = np.sort(observations["obsjd"].to_numpy())
    flares = goes.load_flares()
    flares = flares[(flares["jd_peak"] >= jd.min()) & (flares["jd_peak"] <= jd.max())]
    flares = flares[flares["peak_flux"] >= goes.class_to_flux(min_class)]
    if max_class is not None:
        flares = flares[flares["peak_flux"] < goes.class_to_flux(max_class)]
    flares = flares.reset_index(drop=True)
    covered = coverage.add_coverage(flares, jd)
    # Spectra between the start and the peak: a flare peaking just after the end of the
    # observing day still has its impulsive phase on record.
    start = covered["jd_start"].fillna(covered["jd_peak"] - 10.0 * MINUTE)
    covered["n_rise"] = coverage.count_between(jd, start.to_numpy(), covered["jd_peak"].to_numpy())
    covered = covered[covered["at_peak"] | (covered["n_rise"] >= 3)]
    return covered.sort_values("peak_flux", ascending=False, ignore_index=True)

def clear_sky(
    events: pd.DataFrame,
    steady_obsjd: np.ndarray,
    before_min: float = 26.0,
    window_min: tuple[float, float] = (-8.0, 10.0),
    min_before: int = 12,
    min_window: int = 9,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Flares with a steady, clear sky before their start and around their peak.

    Counts the spectra of ``steady_obsjd`` (see ``quality.stable_obsjd``) from ``before_min`` to
    2 min before the start of the flare, and in ``window_min`` around its peak. The criterion
    uses the signal-to-noise ratio of the spectra alone, never their content, so it can be
    applied before any spectrum is downloaded.
    """
    steady_obsjd = np.asarray(steady_obsjd, dtype=float)
    start = events["jd_start"].fillna(events["jd_peak"] - 10.0 * MINUTE).to_numpy()
    peak = events["jd_peak"].to_numpy()
    before = coverage.count_between(steady_obsjd, start - before_min * MINUTE, start - 2.0 * MINUTE)
    window = coverage.count_between(steady_obsjd, peak + window_min[0] * MINUTE, peak + window_min[1] * MINUTE)
    return pd.Series((before >= min_before) & (window >= min_window), index=events.index)

def control_events(events: pd.DataFrame, max_shift_days: int = 12, margin_min: float = 60.0) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One flare-free epoch per flare: the same time of day on the nearest suitable day.

    A day is suitable when no M or X flare peaks within ``margin_min`` minutes of the shifted
    window and the spectrograph took at least 90 % as many spectra in it as in the window of the
    flare itself (which can be cut short by the start or the end of the observing day). The control
    keeps the class and position of its flare (to pair them) and is named after it.
    """
    observations = np.sort(neid.read_solar_table()["obsjd"].to_numpy())
    flares = goes.load_flares()
    major = np.sort(flares.loc[flares["goes_class"].str[0].isin(["M", "X"]), "jd_peak"].to_numpy())
    rows = []
    for row in events.itertuples():
        start = row.jd_start if row.jd_start == row.jd_start else row.jd_peak - 10.0 * MINUTE
        low, high = start - 30.0 * MINUTE, row.jd_peak + 45.0 * MINUTE
        expected = max(10, coverage.count_between(observations, low, high))
        for shift in (s * d for d in range(1, max_shift_days + 1) for s in (1, -1)):
            quiet = coverage.count_between(major, low + shift - margin_min * MINUTE, high + shift + margin_min * MINUTE) == 0
            observed = coverage.count_between(observations, low + shift, high + shift)
            if quiet and observed >= 0.9 * expected:
                control = row._asdict()
                control.pop("Index", None)
                control.update(jd_start=start + shift, jd_peak=row.jd_peak + shift, parent=event_name(row), shift_days=shift)
                rows.append(control)
                break
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Each flare gets the window from before_min minutes before its start to after_min minutes after its peak. Extracts already on disk are skipped, so the campaign can be stopped and run again.

With kind = "controls" the same windows are fetched on a flare-free day for every flare that already has spectra (see control_events). With usable_only the controls are limited to the flares marked as usable in results/spectral_response.csv.

def run(
    hours: float = 7.5,
    max_files: int = 600,
    step: int = 3,
    before_min: float = 30.0,
    after_min: float = 45.0,
    workers: int = 3,
    min_class: str = "M1.0",
    core_before_min: float = 10.0,
    core_after_min: float = 15.0,
    kind: str = "flares",
    usable_only: bool = False,
    max_class: str | None = None,
    clear_only: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Fetch spectrum extracts flare by flare until the time or the file budget runs out.

    Each flare gets the window from ``before_min`` minutes before its start to ``after_min``
    minutes after its peak. Every spectrum is taken in the core of the flare (from
    ``core_before_min`` minutes before the start to ``core_after_min`` after the peak, where
    things change within a minute) and every ``step``-th one outside it. Extracts already on
    disk are skipped, so the campaign can be stopped and run again.

    With ``kind`` = "controls" the same windows are fetched on a flare-free day for every
    flare that already has spectra (see ``control_events``). With ``usable_only`` the controls
    are limited to the flares marked as usable in ``results/spectral_response.csv``.

    ``max_class`` (exclusive) limits the flares from above. With ``clear_only`` only the flares
    that pass ``clear_sky`` are fetched, and of them only the spectra taken through a steady
    sky: the others would be discarded by the analysis anyway, and each costs 113 MB.
    """
    deadline = time.monotonic() + hours * 3600.0
    events = select_events(min_class, max_class)
    steady = quality.stable_obsjd(neid.read_solar_table()) if clear_only else None
    if clear_only and kind == "flares":
        events = events[clear_sky(events, steady)].reset_index(drop=True)
    root = data_dir() / "spectra"
    if kind == "controls":
        fetched_flares = [len(list((root / event_name(r)).glob("neidL2_*.npz"))) >= 10 for r in events.itertuples()]
        events = control_events(events[fetched_flares])
        if usable_only:
            measured = pd.read_csv(results_dir() / "spectral_response.csv")
            wanted = set(measured.loc[(measured["kind"] == "flare") & measured["usable"], "name"])
            events = events[events["parent"].isin(wanted)].reset_index(drop=True)
    name_of = control_name if kind == "controls" else event_name
    manifest = []
    scratch = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "flinch_spectra"
    scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fetched = 0
    keep_awake(True)
    log(f"campaign: {len(events)} {kind}, budget {hours} h / {max_files} files, step {step}")
    try:
        for row in events.itertuples():
            if time.monotonic() > deadline or fetched >= max_files:
                break
            name = name_of(row)
            start = row.jd_start if row.jd_start == row.jd_start else row.jd_peak - 10.0 * MINUTE
            try:
                files = spectra.list_files(start - before_min * MINUTE, row.jd_peak + after_min * MINUTE)
                if steady is not None:
                    files = files[quality.matches(files["obsjd"].to_numpy(), steady)].reset_index(drop=True)
                core =(files["obsjd"] >= start - core_before_min * MINUTE) & (
                    files["obsjd"] <= row.jd_peak + core_after_min * MINUTE
                )
                files = files[core | (np.arange(len(files)) % step == 0)]
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001  (network trouble: go on with the next flare)
                log(f"{name}: could not list files ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
                continue
            directory = root / name
            directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            todo = [f for f in files.itertuples() if not (directory / (Path(f.l2filename).stem + ".npz")).exists()]
            todo = todo[: max(0, max_files - fetched)]

            def task(item) -> bool:
                if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                    return False
                try:
                    spectra.fetch_one(item.l2filepath, item.l2filename, directory, scratch)
                    return True
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    log(f"{name}: {item.l2filename} failed ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
                    return False

            began = time.monotonic()
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
                done = sum(pool.map(task, todo))
            fetched += done
            manifest.append(
                {
                    "name": name, "kind": kind, "parent": getattr(row, "parent", name),
                    "jd_start": start, "jd_peak": row.jd_peak, "goes_class": row.goes_class,
                    "peak_flux": row.peak_flux, "x_norm": row.x_norm, "y_norm": row.y_norm, "r_norm": row.r_norm,
                }
            )
            write_manifest(manifest)
            have = len(list(directory.glob("neidL2_*.npz")))
            rate = (time.monotonic() - began) / max(done, 1)
            log(f"{name}: +{done} (now {have} of {len(files)}), {rate:.0f} s per file, total fetched {fetched}")
    finally:
        keep_awake(False)
        log(f"campaign finished: {fetched} files fetched")

def own_indices(arrays: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Line-core indices measured on the saved windows of the stitched spectra."""
    out = {}
    for name, (window, centre, half, first, second) in OWN_INDICES.items():
        flux = arrays[f"{window}_flux"]
        if len(flux) == 0:  # every spectrum of the window was rejected
            out[name] = np.array([])
            continue
        wave = arrays[f"{window}_wave"][0]
        core = np.abs(wave - centre) <= half
        reference = ((wave >= first[0]) & (wave <= first[1])) | ((wave >= second[0]) & (wave <= second[1]))
        out[name] = flux[:, core].mean(axis=1) / flux[:, reference].mean(axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

def event_table(directory: Path, jd_start: float, jd_peak: float, keep_obsjd=None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per spectrum of a flare window, with time relative to the flare and the line shape.

    ``keep_obsjd`` is an optional sorted array of exposure start times; spectra not in it (to
    0.2 s) are dropped. Pass ``quality.stable_obsjd`` to leave out those taken through cloud.
    """
    table, arrays = spectra.load_window(directory)
    if keep_obsjd is not None and len(table):
        kept = quality.matches(table["obsjd"].to_numpy(), keep_obsjd)
        table = table[kept].reset_index(drop=True)
        arrays = {key: value[kept] for key, value in arrays.items()}
    with np.load(next(Path(directory).glob("neidL2_*.npz"))) as first:
        ccf_start, ccf_step = float(first["ccfstart"]), float(first["ccfstep"])
    table = pd.concat([table, lineshape.measure(arrays["ccf"], ccf_start, ccf_step), own_indices(arrays)], axis=1)
    table["min_peak"] = (table["jd"] - jd_peak) / MINUTE

def changes(table: pd.DataFrame, baseline_end_min: float = -2.0, detrend: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Change of each quantity with respect to the spectra taken before the flare start.

    Indices and line-shape parameters are relative changes (parts per thousand or per million);
    the bisector span and the velocity are differences in m/s. With ``detrend`` a straight line
    fitted to the pre-flare spectra is removed instead of their mean (the slow drift with the
    height of the Sun), at the price of a larger error when extrapolated through the flare.
    ``<column>_sigma`` is the scatter of the pre-flare values about that baseline.
    """
    before = table["min_start"] < baseline_end_min
    out = table[["jd", "min_peak", "min_start"]].copy()
    out["pre_flare"] = before
    time = table["min_start"].to_numpy()
    for column, _, unit in QUANTITIES:
        values = table[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        if before.sum() >= (4 if detrend else 2):
            if detrend:
                baseline = np.polyval(np.polyfit(time[before], values[before], 1), time)
            else:
                baseline = np.full(len(values), values[before].mean())
            change = (values / baseline - 1.0) * SCALE[unit] if unit in SCALE else values - baseline
            out[column] = change
            out[f"{column}_sigma"] = float(np.std(change[before.to_numpy()], ddof=2 if detrend else 1))
        else:
            out[column] = np.nan
            out[f"{column}_sigma"] = np.nan
    return out

def event_response(change: pd.DataFrame, window_min: tuple[float, float] = (-8.0, 10.0)) -> dict:
    """Mean change of each quantity around the X-ray peak, with its error.

    The window is in minutes from the peak. The error combines the scatter of the pre-flare
    spectra over the number of spectra in the window and in the baseline.
    """
    inside = (change["min_peak"] >= window_min[0]) & (change["min_peak"] <= window_min[1]) & ~change["pre_flare"]
    n_window, n_before = int(inside.sum()), int(change["pre_flare"].sum())
    out = {"n_window": n_window, "n_before": n_before}
    for column, _, _ in QUANTITIES:
        sigma = float(change[f"{column}_sigma"].iloc[0])
        if n_window >= 2 and n_before >= 3 and np.isfinite(sigma):
            out[column] = float(change.loc[inside, column].mean())
            out[f"{column}_err"] = sigma * float(np.sqrt(1.0 / n_window + 1.0 / n_before))
        else:
            out[column] = np.nan
            out[f"{column}_err"] = np.nan
    return out

    (class, flux, position, kind) are carried over.

    rows = []

        if len(list(directory.glob("neidL2_*.npz"))) < 8:

        if len(table) < 8:
            continue
        row.update(event_response(changes(table, detrend=detrend), window_min))
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def normalize(velocity: np.ndarray, ccf: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """CCF divided by its continuum, taken as the mean of both wings."""
    centre = velocity[np.argmin(ccf)]
    distance = np.abs(velocity - centre)
    wings = (distance >= CONTINUUM_KMS[0]) & (distance <= CONTINUUM_KMS[1])
    return ccf / ccf[wings].mean()

def gaussian_fit(velocity: np.ndarray, profile: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Centre (km/s), depth and full width at half maximum (km/s) of an inverted Gaussian."""
    guess = velocity[np.argmin(profile)]
    use = np.abs(velocity - guess) <= FIT_HALF_WIDTH_KMS
    v, y = velocity[use], profile[use]

    def residual(parameters):
        centre, depth, sigma, level = parameters
        return level - depth * np.exp(-0.5 * ((v - centre) / sigma) ** 2) - y

    fit = least_squares(residual, [guess, 1.0 - y.min(), 3.5, 1.0])
    centre, depth, sigma, _ = fit.x
    return float(centre), float(depth), float(2.3548200450309493 * abs(sigma))

def bisector_span(velocity: np.ndarray, profile: np.ndarray, top=(0.10, 0.40), bottom=(0.60, 0.90)) -> float:
    """Bisector inverse slope in m/s: mean bisector near the top of the line minus near the bottom.

    The levels are fractions of the line depth, measured from the continuum.
    """
    # Work on a finely resampled profile: taking the minimum and the wings from the 0.25 km/s
    # samples makes the span jump by more than 1 m/s whenever the lowest sample changes.
    coarse_min = velocity[int(np.argmin(profile))]
    fine_v = np.arange(coarse_min - 15.0, coarse_min + 15.0, 0.005)
    fine_p = CubicSpline(velocity, profile)(fine_v)
    i_min = int(np.argmin(fine_p))
    depth = 1.0 - fine_p[i_min]
    levels = 1.0 - depth * np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 91)
    blue_v, blue_p = fine_v[: i_min + 1][::-1], fine_p[: i_min + 1][::-1]  # from the core outwards
    red_v, red_p = fine_v[i_min:], fine_p[i_min:]
    # Keep the monotonic part of each wing, so that np.interp gets increasing abscissae.
    blue_end = int(np.argmax(blue_p >= levels[0])) + 1 if np.any(blue_p >= levels[0]) else len(blue_p)
    red_end = int(np.argmax(red_p >= levels[0])) + 1 if np.any(red_p >= levels[0]) else len(red_p)
    bisector = 0.5 * (
        np.interp(levels, blue_p[:blue_end], blue_v[:blue_end]) + np.interp(levels, red_p[:red_end], red_v[:red_end])
    )
    fraction = (1.0 - levels) / depth
    upper = bisector[(fraction >= top[0]) & (fraction <= top[1])].mean()
    lower = bisector[(fraction >= bottom[0]) & (fraction <= bottom[1])].mean()
    return float((upper - lower) * 1000.0)

def measure(ccfs: np.ndarray, start: float, step: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shape parameters of each CCF: centre (m/s), depth, width (km/s), area (km/s) and bisector span (m/s)."""
    velocity = velocity_grid(start, step, ccfs.shape[1])
    rows = []
    for ccf in ccfs:
        profile = normalize(velocity, ccf)
        centre, depth, fwhm = gaussian_fit(velocity, profile)
        near = np.abs(velocity - centre) <= CONTINUUM_KMS[0]
        rows.append(
            {
                "ccf_rv_ms": centre * 1000.0,
                "ccf_depth": depth,
                "ccf_fwhm_kms": fwhm,
                "ccf_area_kms": float(np.sum(1.0 - profile[near]) * step),
                "ccf_bis_ms": bisector_span(velocity, profile),
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def shifted_profiles(ccfs: np.ndarray, start: float, step: float, half_width_kms: float = 15.0):
    """Normalized CCFs resampled on a common grid centred on each line (removes velocity shifts).

    Returns the grid (km/s from the line centre) and the array (spectra, grid points).
    """
    velocity = velocity_grid(start, step, ccfs.shape[1])
    grid = np.arange(-half_width_kms, half_width_kms + 0.5 * step, step)
    out = np.empty((len(ccfs), len(grid)))
    for k, ccf in enumerate(ccfs):
        profile = normalize(velocity, ccf)
        centre, _, _ = gaussian_fit(velocity, profile)
        # A cubic spline: linear interpolation of a line sampled every 0.25 km/s is wrong by up
        # to a few parts in 10^4 at the core, more than the changes looked for.
        out[k] = CubicSpline(velocity, profile)(centre + grid)
    return grid, out

def stable_obsjd(table: pd.DataFrame, snr_tolerance: float = 0.01) -> np.ndarray:
    """Exposure start times (sorted) of the spectra taken through a steady, clear sky.

    ``snr_tolerance`` of its running median. Unlike ``good`` it does not drop whole days, so it

def matches(obsjd, keep_obsjd, tolerance: float = 2.0e-6) -> np.ndarray:
    """Which exposure start times are in the sorted array ``keep_obsjd``, to 0.2 s by default."""
    obsjd = np.asarray(obsjd, dtype=float)
    keep_obsjd = np.asarray(keep_obsjd, dtype=float)
    if len(keep_obsjd) == 0:
        return np.zeros(len(obsjd), dtype=bool)
    after = np.clip(np.searchsorted(keep_obsjd, obsjd), 0, len(keep_obsjd) - 1)
    before = np.clip(after - 1, 0, len(keep_obsjd) - 1)
    nearest = np.minimum(np.abs(keep_obsjd[after] - obsjd), np.abs(keep_obsjd[before] - obsjd))
    return nearest < tolerance

Returns the residuals (NaN on dropped days), the scatter of each day and the updated mask of good points.

def detrend_days(
    jd: np.ndarray,
    rv: np.ndarray,
    days: np.ndarray,
    good: np.ndarray,
    order: int = 2,
    clip: float = 5.0,
    min_points: int = 40,
    max_day_sigma: float = 1.5,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Subtract a polynomial from the velocities of each day; the arrays must be sorted in time.

    The polynomial of degree ``order`` is fitted to the good points of the day, dropping those
    beyond ``clip`` robust sigmas until the selection settles. Days left with fewer than
    ``min_points`` good points, or with a robust scatter above ``max_day_sigma``, are dropped
    whole. Returns the residuals (NaN on dropped days), the scatter of each day and the updated
    mask of good points.
    """
    good = np.array(good, dtype=bool)  # writable copy
    residual = np.full(len(jd), np.nan)
    day_sigma = np.full(len(jd), np.nan)
    boundaries = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(days)) + 1
    for lo, hi in zip(np.r_[0, boundaries], np.r_[boundaries, len(days)]):
        mask = good[lo:hi].copy()
        if mask.sum() < min_points:
            good[lo:hi] = False
            continue
        hours = (jd[lo:hi] - jd[lo:hi][mask].mean()) * 24.0
        velocity = rv[lo:hi]
        for _ in range(6):
            fit = np.polyfit(hours[mask], velocity[mask], order)
            r = velocity - np.polyval(fit, hours)
            sigma = robust_sigma(r[mask])
            updated = good[lo:hi] & (np.abs(r) < clip * sigma)
            if updated.sum() < min_points or np.array_equal(updated, mask):
                mask = updated
                break
            mask = updated
        if mask.sum() < min_points:
            good[lo:hi] = False
            continue
        day_sigma[lo:hi] = robust_sigma(r[mask])
        if day_sigma[lo] > max_day_sigma:
            good[lo:hi] = False
            continue
        residual[lo:hi] = r
        good[lo:hi] = mask
    return residual, day_sigma, good

Added columns:

jd mid-exposure Julian date (UTC). day integer UT day number. snr_rel signal-to-noise ratio divided by its running median over snr_window spectra. res velocity minus the polynomial of degree order fitted to the good points of the day (m/s). day_sigma robust scatter of the good residuals of the day (m/s). good passes every cut.

Cuts: a valid velocity error below max_rv_err_ms; a signal-to-noise ratio above min_snr and within snr_tolerance of its running median (passing clouds lower it and bias the velocity); a residual within clip robust sigmas of the daily fit; at least min_points good spectra in the day; and a daily scatter below max_day_sigma (the median day has 0.8 m/s; days of broken cloud reach tens of m/s and are dropped whole).

def prepare(
    table: pd.DataFrame,
    snr_window: int = 31,
    snr_tolerance: float = 0.01,
    max_rv_err_ms: float = 1.0,
    min_snr: float = 50.0,
    order: int = 2,
    clip: float = 5.0,
    min_points: int = 40,
    max_day_sigma: float = 1.5,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag good observations and subtract a polynomial trend from each day.

    Added columns:

    ``jd``      mid-exposure Julian date (UTC).
    ``day``     integer UT day number.
    ``snr_rel`` signal-to-noise ratio divided by its running median over ``snr_window`` spectra.
    ``res``     velocity minus the polynomial of degree ``order`` fitted to the good points of the day (m/s).
    ``day_sigma`` robust scatter of the good residuals of the day (m/s).
    ``good``    passes every cut.

    Cuts: a valid velocity error below ``max_rv_err_ms``; a signal-to-noise ratio above
    ``min_snr`` and within ``snr_tolerance`` of its running median (passing clouds lower it and
    bias the velocity); a residual within ``clip`` robust sigmas of the daily fit; at least
    ``min_points`` good spectra in the day; and a daily scatter below ``max_day_sigma`` (the
    median day has 0.8 m/s; days of broken cloud reach tens of m/s and are dropped whole).
    """
    out = table.sort_values("obsjd", ignore_index=True).copy()
    exposure = out["exptime"].where(out["exptime"] > 0, DEFAULT_EXPOSURE_S) if "exptime" in out else DEFAULT_EXPOSURE_S
    out["jd"] = out["obsjd"] + 0.5 * exposure / 86400.0
    out["day"] = np.floor(out["jd"] - 0.5).astype(np.int64)

    valid = (
        np.isfinite(out["rv_ms"])
        & (out["rv_err_ms"] > 0.0)
        & (out["rv_err_ms"] < max_rv_err_ms)
        & (out["extsnr"] > min_snr)
    )
    snr = out["extsnr"].where(valid)
    reference = snr.groupby(out["day"]).transform(
        lambda s: s.rolling(snr_window, center=True, min_periods=max(3, snr_window // 4)).median()
    )
    out["snr_rel"] = snr / reference
    good = np.array(valid & ((out["snr_rel"] - 1.0).abs() <= snr_tolerance), dtype=bool)  # writable copy

    residual, day_sigma, good = detrend_days(
        out["jd"].to_numpy(), out["rv_ms"].to_numpy(), out["day"].to_numpy(), good, order, clip, min_points, max_day_sigma
    )
    out["res"] = residual
    out["day_sigma"] = day_sigma
    out["good"] = good
    return out

class Series:
    """Time-sorted values with prefix sums, for fast means over many windows."""

    def __init__(self, jd, values):
        jd = np.asarray(jd, dtype=float)
        values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
        order = np.argsort(jd, kind="stable")
        self.jd = jd[order]
        self._cumulative = np.r_[0.0, np.cumsum(values[order])]

    def window(self, low, high) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Number of points and mean value in each closed interval [low, high] (NaN if empty)."""
        first = np.searchsorted(self.jd, low, side="left")
        last = np.searchsorted(self.jd, high, side="right")
        count = last - first
        total = self._cumulative[last] - self._cumulative[first]
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            mean = np.where(count > 0, total / np.maximum(count, 1), np.nan)
        return count, mean

def measure(events: pd.DataFrame, series: Series, windows: Windows = Windows()) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Velocity change of each event (m/s) with respect to its own pre-event baseline.

    ``delta``            mean in the signal window minus mean in the pre-event window.
    ``delta_two_sided``  the same, with the average of the pre and post windows as baseline
                         (cancels a linear trend, but is biased if the response outlasts the peak).
    ``delta_decay``      mean in the decay window minus mean in the pre-event window.
    ``measured``         enough points before and during the event: the minimum number and at
                         least ``min_fraction`` of those expected, so that windows riddled
                         with rejected spectra (passing clouds) are left out.
    """
    start, peak = event_times(events)
    n_pre, pre = series.window(start + windows.pre[0] * MINUTE, start + windows.pre[1] * MINUTE)
    n_signal, signal = series.window(start, peak + windows.signal_after_peak * MINUTE)
    n_post, post = series.window(peak + windows.post[0] * MINUTE, peak + windows.post[1] * MINUTE)
    n_decay, decay = series.window(peak + windows.decay[0] * MINUTE, peak + windows.decay[1] * MINUTE)
    out = events.copy()
    out["rise_min"] = (peak - start) / MINUTE
    out["n_pre"], out["n_signal"], out["n_post"], out["n_decay"] = n_pre, n_signal, n_post, n_decay
    out["baseline"] = pre
    out["delta"] = signal - pre
    out["delta_two_sided"] = signal - 0.5 * (pre + post)
    out["delta_decay"] = decay - pre
    per_minute = windows.min_fraction * 60.0 / windows.cadence_s
    need_pre = np.maximum(windows.min_pre, per_minute * (windows.pre[1] - windows.pre[0]))
    need_signal = np.maximum(windows.min_signal, per_minute * ((peak - start) / MINUTE + windows.signal_after_peak))
    need_post = np.maximum(windows.min_post, per_minute * (windows.post[1] - windows.post[0]))
    out["measured"] = (n_pre >= need_pre) & (n_signal >= need_signal)
    out["measured_two_sided"] = out["measured"] & (n_post >= need_post)
    return out

def profiles(events: pd.DataFrame, series: Series, edges_min, windows: Windows = Windows()) -> np.ndarray:
    """Mean residual of each event in time bins relative to its peak, minus its pre-event mean.

    Returns an array (events, bins); empty bins are NaN.
    """
    start, peak = event_times(events)
    _, pre = series.window(start + windows.pre[0] * MINUTE, start + windows.pre[1] * MINUTE)
    edges = np.asarray(edges_min, dtype=float)
    out = np.full((len(events), len(edges) - 1), np.nan)
    for k in range(len(edges) - 1):
        # Half-open bins: nudge the upper edge so that a point is never counted twice.
        _, mean = series.window(peak + edges[k] * MINUTE, peak + edges[k + 1] * MINUTE - 1e-9)
        out[:, k] = mean - pre
    return out

A candidate is kept when no major flare peaks between margin_min minutes before its start and margin_min minutes after its peak. rank is a random order within each flare.

def draw_controls(
    flares: pd.DataFrame,
    major_peaks_jd,
    max_shift_days: int = 15,
    margin_min: float = 45.0,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Candidate flare-free epochs for each flare, at the same time of day on nearby days.

    Every flare is shifted by whole days (so that the Sun is at the same height and the
    instrument in the same state of its daily cycle) up to ``max_shift_days`` either way. A
    candidate is kept when no major flare peaks between ``margin_min`` minutes before its start
    and ``margin_min`` minutes after its peak. ``rank`` is a random order within each flare.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    start, peak = event_times(flares)
    shifts = np.r_[-np.arange(1, max_shift_days + 1), np.arange(1, max_shift_days + 1)].astype(float)
    major = np.sort(np.asarray(major_peaks_jd, dtype=float))
    shifted_start = (start[:, None] + shifts[None, :]).ravel()
    shifted_peak = (peak[:, None] + shifts[None, :]).ravel()
    parent = np.repeat(np.arange(len(flares)), len(shifts))
    low = shifted_start - margin_min * MINUTE
    high = shifted_peak + margin_min * MINUTE
    quiet = np.searchsorted(major, high, side="right") == np.searchsorted(major, low, side="left")
    controls = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "parent": parent[quiet],
            "shift_days": np.tile(shifts, len(flares))[quiet],
            "jd_start": shifted_start[quiet],
            "jd_peak": shifted_peak[quiet],
            "rank": rng.random(int(quiet.sum())),
        }
    )
    for column in ("goes_class", "peak_flux", "x_norm", "y_norm", "r_norm"):
        if column in flares:
            controls[column] = flares[column].to_numpy()[controls["parent"].to_numpy()]
    return controls

Least-squares amplitude a of the model delta = a * weight and its error.

sigma is the noise of one measurement (taken from the control sample). With weight = peak flux in units of an X1 flare, a is the response to an X1 flare; with weight = flux times the position across the disc, it is the rotational signature.

def scaled_amplitude(delta, weight, sigma: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Least-squares amplitude ``a`` of the model ``delta = a * weight`` and its error.

    ``sigma`` is the noise of one measurement (taken from the control sample). With
    ``weight`` = peak flux in units of an X1 flare, ``a`` is the response to an X1 flare; with
    ``weight`` = flux times the position across the disc, it is the rotational signature.
    """
    delta = np.asarray(delta, dtype=float)
    weight = np.asarray(weight, dtype=float)
    keep = np.isfinite(delta) & np.isfinite(weight)
    norm = float(np.sum(weight[keep] ** 2))
    if norm == 0.0:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    return float(np.sum(weight[keep] * delta[keep]) / norm), float(sigma / np.sqrt(norm))

Series of squared residuals and of squared differences between consecutive spectra.

The mean square over a window measures the power of the fluctuations, which at this cadence is dominated by the solar five-minute oscillations. The squared difference of two consecutive spectra (kept only when they are less than max_gap_s apart, and dated at their mid-point) weights the high-frequency end, up to the Nyquist frequency of 6 mHz.

def power_series(jd, values, max_gap_s: float = 125.0) -> tuple[Series, Series]:
    """Series of squared residuals and of squared differences between consecutive spectra.

    The mean square over a window measures the power of the fluctuations, which at this
    cadence is dominated by the solar five-minute oscillations. The squared difference of two
    consecutive spectra (kept only when they are less than ``max_gap_s`` apart, and dated at
    their mid-point) weights the high-frequency end, up to the Nyquist frequency of 6 mHz.
    """
    jd = np.asarray(jd, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    order = np.argsort(jd, kind="stable")
    jd, values = jd[order], values[order]
    consecutive = np.diff(jd) * 86400.0 < max_gap_s
    return (
        Series(jd, values**2),
        Series(0.5 * (jd[1:] + jd[:-1])[consecutive], np.diff(values)[consecutive] ** 2),
    )

Change of the fluctuation power of each event, as natural logarithms of power ratios.

log_power mean square after the peak (the post window) over the pre-event one. log_power_hf the same for the squared differences of consecutive spectra. power_measured enough points in both windows.

def measure_power(
    events: pd.DataFrame, squares: Series, differences: Series, windows: Windows = Windows()
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Change of the fluctuation power of each event, as natural logarithms of power ratios.

    ``log_power``     mean square after the peak (the ``post`` window) over the pre-event one.
    ``log_power_hf``  the same for the squared differences of consecutive spectra.
    ``power_measured`` enough points in both windows.
    """
    start, peak = event_times(events)
    out = events.copy()
    need = max(windows.min_pre, windows.min_post)
    measured = np.ones(len(events), dtype=bool)
    for column, series in (("log_power", squares), ("log_power_hf", differences)):
        n_pre, pre = series.window(start + windows.pre[0] * MINUTE, start + windows.pre[1] * MINUTE)
        n_post, post = series.window(peak + windows.post[0] * MINUTE, peak + windows.post[1] * MINUTE)
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            out[column] = np.log(post / pre)
        measured &= (n_pre >= need) & (n_post >= need)
    out["power_measured"] = measured & np.isfinite(out["log_power"]) & np.isfinite(out["log_power_hf"])
    return out

def matched_null(controls: pd.DataFrame, statistic, draws: int = 2000, seed: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Distribution of ``statistic`` over samples made of one random control per flare."""

def summarize(flares: pd.DataFrame, controls: pd.DataFrame, column: str = "delta") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mean of ``column`` for flares and controls, per class band and for the whole sample."""
    rows = []
    bands_f = flares["goes_class"].map(coverage.class_band)
    bands_c = controls["goes_class"].map(coverage.class_band)
    for band in (*BANDS, "all"):
        f = flares[column] if band == "all" else flares.loc[bands_f == band, column]
        c = controls[column] if band == "all" else controls.loc[bands_c == band, column]
        mean_f, sem_f, n_f = epoch.mean_and_error(f)
        mean_c, sem_c, n_c = epoch.mean_and_error(c)
        difference = mean_f - mean_c
        error = float(np.hypot(sem_f, sem_c))
        rows.append(
            {
                "band": band,
                "n_flares": n_f,
                "flare_mean": mean_f,
                "flare_sem": sem_f,
                "flare_std": float(np.nanstd(f, ddof=1)) if n_f > 1 else np.nan,
                "n_controls": n_c,
                "control_mean": mean_c,
                "control_sem": sem_c,
                "control_std": float(np.nanstd(c, ddof=1)) if n_c > 1 else np.nan,
                "difference": difference,
                "error": error,
                "z": difference / error if error > 0 else np.nan,
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def inject(observations: pd.DataFrame, events: pd.DataFrame, amplitude_ms: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Copy of the raw table with a box of ``amplitude_ms`` added in the signal window of each event."""
    out = observations.copy()
    exposure = out["exptime"].where(out["exptime"] > 0, quality.DEFAULT_EXPOSURE_S) if "exptime" in out else quality.DEFAULT_EXPOSURE_S
    jd = (out["obsjd"] + 0.5 * exposure / 86400.0).to_numpy()
    order = np.argsort(jd)
    start, peak = epoch.event_times(events)
    first = np.searchsorted(jd[order], start, side="left")
    last = np.searchsorted(jd[order], peak + epoch.Windows().signal_after_peak * MINUTE, side="right")
    added = np.zeros(len(out))
    for a, b in zip(first, last):
        added[order[a:b]] = amplitude_ms
    out["rv_ms"] = out["rv_ms"] + added
    return out

def run(per_flare: int = 10, seed: int = 0, injection_ms: float = 1.0) -> dict:
    """Run the pilot; returns the tables that the command line prints and writes."""
    raw = neid.read_solar_table()
    observations = quality.prepare(raw)
    good = observations[observations["good"]]
    series = epoch.Series(good["jd"], good["res"])
    squares, differences = epoch.power_series(good["jd"], good["res"])

    all_flares = goes.load_flares()
    sample = major_flare_sample(all_flares, raw["obsjd"].to_numpy())
    flares = epoch.measure(sample, series)
    flares = flares[flares["measured"]].reset_index(drop=True)
    flares = epoch.measure_power(flares, squares, differences)

    candidates = epoch.draw_controls(flares, sample["jd_peak"].to_numpy(), seed=seed)
    controls = epoch.select_controls(epoch.measure(candidates, series), per_flare=per_flare)
    controls = epoch.measure_power(controls, squares, differences)

    noise = float(controls["delta"].std(ddof=1))

    def power(column):
        return lambda e: float(e.loc[e["power_measured"], column].mean())

    statistics = {
        "mean change (m/s)": lambda e: float(e["delta"].mean()),
        "change per X1 flare (m/s)": lambda e: epoch.scaled_amplitude(e["delta"], flux_weight(e), noise)[0],
        "rotation term per X1 at the limb (m/s)": lambda e: epoch.scaled_amplitude(
            e["delta"], rotation_weight(e), noise
        )[0],
        "mean change in the decay phase (m/s)": lambda e: float(e["delta_decay"].mean()),
        "log power ratio after/before": power("log_power"),
        "log power ratio, high frequency": power("log_power_hf"),
    }
    tests = []
    for name, statistic in statistics.items():
        null = matched_null(controls, statistic, seed=seed)
        value = statistic(flares)
        centre, spread = float(null.mean()), float(null.std(ddof=1))
        tests.append(
            {
                "statistic": name,
                "flares": value,
                "null_mean": centre,
                "null_std": spread,
                "excess": value - centre,
                "z": (value - centre) / spread,
                "p_two_sided": float(np.mean(np.abs(null - centre) >= abs(value - centre))),
                "limit_95": abs(value - centre) + 1.645 * spread,  # one-sided 95 % limit on the size of the excess
            }
        )

    # Injection test: add a known box to the raw velocities at one control epoch per day (so that
    # no injected box falls in the baseline of another) and measure it back through the whole chain.
    control_day = np.floor(controls["jd_peak"] - 0.5)
    isolated = controls.groupby(control_day).sample(1, random_state=seed)
    injected = quality.prepare(inject(raw, isolated, injection_ms))
    injected_good = injected[injected["good"]]
    recovered = epoch.measure(isolated, epoch.Series(injected_good["jd"], injected_good["res"]))
    kept = recovered["measured"].to_numpy()
    efficiency = float((recovered.loc[kept, "delta"].mean() - isolated.loc[kept, "delta"].mean()) / injection_ms)

    profiles = []
    for label, minimum in PROFILE_SUBSETS:
        profiles.append(stacked_profile(flares[flares["peak_flux"] >= minimum], series, label, "flares"))
        profiles.append(stacked_profile(controls[controls["peak_flux"] >= minimum], series, label, "controls"))
    return {
        "observations": observations,
        "flares": flares,
        "controls": controls,
        "summary": summarize(flares, controls),
        "summary_two_sided": summarize(
            flares[flares["measured_two_sided"]], controls[controls["measured_two_sided"]], "delta_two_sided"
        ),
        "tests": pd.DataFrame(tests),
        "profiles": pd.concat(profiles, ignore_index=True),
        "numbers": {
            "spectra": len(observations),
            "good_spectra": int(observations["good"].sum()),
            "point_sigma_ms": quality.robust_sigma(good["res"].to_numpy()),
            "event_noise_ms": noise,
            "injection_ms": injection_ms,
            "injection_efficiency": efficiency,
        },
    }

def rotation_fraction(events: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    """Line-of-sight rotation velocity at the flare position, as a fraction of the equatorial one.

    West (receding) positive. Uses the differential rotation law with the sine of the latitude
    approximated by the height on the disc; NaN outside the disc.
    """
    x = events["x_norm"].where(events["r_norm"] < 1.05).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    y2 = np.clip(events["y_norm"].to_numpy(dtype=float), -1.0, 1.0) ** 2
    return x * (1.0 - 0.120 * y2 - 0.166 * y2**2)

def signal_window(events: pd.DataFrame, estimator: str) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Limits (Julian dates) of the window in which the velocity change is measured."""
    start, peak = epoch.event_times(events)

    if estimator == "rise":  # the default of the pilot

    if estimator == "start":

    if estimator == "peak":
        return peak - 5.0 * MINUTE, peak + 5.0 * MINUTE
    raise ValueError(estimator)

def window_delta(
    events: pd.DataFrame,
    series: epoch.Series,
    estimator: str,
    cadence_s: float = 83.0,
    min_pre: int = MIN_PRE,
    min_signal: int = MIN_SIGNAL,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Mean in the signal window minus mean in the pre-flare window (NaN when under-sampled).

    A window counts when it holds at least 70 % of the points expected at the cadence
    ``cadence_s`` of the instrument, and never fewer than ``min_pre`` or ``min_signal``.
    """
    start, _ = epoch.event_times(events)
    low, high = signal_window(events, estimator)
    n_pre, pre = series.window(start + PRE[0] * MINUTE, start + PRE[1] * MINUTE)
    n_signal, signal = series.window(low, high)
    expected = 0.7 * (high - low) * 86400.0 / cadence_s
    ok = (n_pre >= max(min_pre, 0.7 * (PRE[1] - PRE[0]) * 60.0 / cadence_s)) & (n_signal >= np.maximum(min_signal, expected))
    return np.where(ok, signal - pre, np.nan)

def local_delta(events: pd.DataFrame, jd: np.ndarray, rv: np.ndarray, order: int = 1) -> np.ndarray:
    """Velocity change against a background fitted locally on both sides of each event.

    A polynomial is fitted to the velocities from 60 to 10 minutes before the start and from 30
    to 90 minutes after the peak, leaving out the interval that the flare may affect; the
    change is the mean of velocity minus fit from the start to 2 minutes after the peak.
    """
    start, peak = epoch.event_times(events)
    out = np.full(len(events), np.nan)
    for k, (t0, t1) in enumerate(zip(start, peak)):
        before = (jd >= t0 - 60.0 * MINUTE) & (jd <= t0 - 10.0 * MINUTE)
        after = (jd >= t1 + 30.0 * MINUTE) & (jd <= t1 + 90.0 * MINUTE)
        during = (jd >= t0) & (jd <= t1 + 2.0 * MINUTE)
        if before.sum() >= 20 and after.sum() >= 20 and during.sum() >= MIN_SIGNAL:
            side = before | after
            hours = (jd - t0) * 24.0
            fit = np.polyfit(hours[side], rv[side], order)
            out[k] = float(np.mean(rv[during] - np.polyval(fit, hours[during])))
    return out

def paired(flare_delta: np.ndarray, controls: pd.DataFrame, control_delta: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:

Label of the active region of each flare, from positions alone.

Two flares belong to the same region when they are within days of each other and within lon_deg in Carrington longitude and lat_deg in latitude; flares without heliographic coordinates (at the limb) are grouped with the flares of their day. def region_groups(flares: pd.DataFrame, lon_deg: float = 10.0, lat_deg: float = 8.0, days: float = 14.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Label of the active region of each flare, from positions alone.

    Two flares belong to the same region when they are within ``days`` of each other and within
    ``lon_deg`` in Carrington longitude and ``lat_deg`` in latitude; flares without heliographic
    coordinates (at the limb) are grouped with the flares of their day. Groups are closed under
    these links, so a region followed across the disc stays one group.
    """
    jd = flares["jd_peak"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    lon = flares["car_lon"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    lat = flares["lat"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    day = np.floor(jd - 0.5)
    label = np.arange(len(flares))

    def find(i):
        while label[i] != i:
            label[i] = label[label[i]]
            i = label[i]
        return i

    for i in range(len(flares)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(flares)):
            located = np.isfinite(lon[i]) and np.isfinite(lon[j]) and np.isfinite(lat[i]) and np.isfinite(lat[j])
            if located:
                apart = abs(lon[i] - lon[j]) % 360.0
                same = abs(jd[i] - jd[j]) < days and min(apart, 360.0 - apart) < lon_deg and abs(lat[i] - lat[j]) < lat_deg
            else:
                same = day[i] == day[j]
            if same:
                label[find(i)] = find(j)
    return np.array([find(i) for i in range(len(flares))])

def day_bootstrap(values: dict[str, np.ndarray], days: np.ndarray, statistics: dict, draws: int = 4000, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Value and standard error of each statistic, resampling observing days with replacement."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    unique, inverse = np.unique(days, return_inverse=True)
    members = [np.flatnonzero(inverse == k) for k in range(len(unique))]
    out = {name: [function(values)] for name, function in statistics.items()}
    for _ in range(draws):
        rows = np.concatenate([members[k] for k in rng.integers(len(unique), size=len(unique))])
        resampled = {key: array[rows] for key, array in values.items()}
        for name, function in statistics.items():
            out[name].append(function(resampled))
    return {name: (results[0], float(np.nanstd(results[1:], ddof=1))) for name, results in out.items()}

def analyse(flares: pd.DataFrame, d: np.ndarray, label: str, seed: int = 0, by_region: bool = False) -> dict:
    """One row of the robustness table for the paired changes ``d``.

    The bootstrap resamples observing days, or active regions with ``by_region`` (the column
    ``days`` then counts regions).
    """
    keep = np.isfinite(d)
    if keep.sum() < 2:  # nothing to resample (for instance, a sample without X-class flares)
        row = {"configuration": label, "flares": int(keep.sum()), "days": int(keep.sum())}
        for name in STATISTICS:
            row[name], row[f"{name}_err"] = np.nan, np.nan
        return row
    values = {"d": d[keep], "flux": pilot.flux_weight(flares)[keep], "rot": rotation_fraction(flares)[keep]}
    days = np.floor(flares["jd_peak"].to_numpy()[keep] - 0.5)
    if by_region:
        days = region_groups(flares)[keep]
    result = day_bootstrap(values, days, STATISTICS, seed=seed)
    row = {"configuration": label, "flares": int(keep.sum()), "days": int(len(np.unique(days)))}
    for name, (value, error) in result.items():
        row[name], row[f"{name}_err"] = value, error
    return row
